channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Oct 16–22
item.description: The week's most consequential meeting is Telluride's HARC session on Tuesday, October 21, where the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Rd — a large Town-owned project in an Accommodations 2 zone — goes before the commission as two continued public hearings covering four buildings. Norwood's Planning and Zoning Commission also meets Monday with a Land Use Code Update and Master Plan Update on the table, foundational decisions that will shape what gets built there for years. On the community side, the San Miguel Watershed Forum on Tuesday and the water-in-the-West talk Thursday are worth your time if water is on your mind — and around here, it always should be.

item.title: [Fri, Oct 16] 17th Telluride Horror Show
item.description:
🎫 KOTO
The Telluride Horror Show returns for its 17th edition October 16-18, 2026. One of the highest-attended genre film fests in the world, the Horror Show attracts the latest & best genre films from around the globe and attendees from all over the country for an incredible gathering of die-hard horror fans in the world-famous mountain resort town of Telluride, Colorado. For three packed days, experience an exciting mix of horror, suspense, thriller, dark fantasy & sci-fi and dark comedy in Telluride’s unique theaters. The festival line-up showcases feature films & short films from new and established talent, special programs, guests, and events. If you love horror, then don't miss Colorado's first and longest-running horror film festival!

item.title: [Tue, Oct 20] San Miguel Watershed Forum – How to Fund Your Water Project
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Science & Innovation Center, TELLURIDE
The San Miguel Watershed Coalition relies on engagement and support from our community to achieve our mission of promoting a healthy San Miguel River Basin, both environmentally and economically. The Coalition has the unique ability to work across geographies and political boundaries, to partner and magnify the impact of individual stakeholders and projects, and to build watershed initiatives that are greater than the sum of their parts.To put it simply, the Watershed Coalition connects its partners to resources to fund projects. In the face of historic drought across the West, it has never been more important to stand together for the future of the San Miguel River. Please join us for the 2026 San Miguel Watershed Forum at 9:00 AM on October 20 at the Telluride Science and Innovation Center. Attendees will learn about the Coalition’s current work, funding opportunities for water projects, and collaboration opportunities. …

item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride
Famed writer and nascent poet Rob Schultheis of Lawson Hill will join poet performer and writer Elle Metrick of Wrights Mesa for the October 20 th session of Stories & Poems at the Wilkinson Public Library at 5:15 pm. MDT “I have been a fan of Rob’s work since I moved to Telluride in the early ‘80s,” said Art Goodtimes, Talking Gourds director. “Elle has been a poet performer colleague and Norwood area friend for over 20 years. It should be a delightful evening.” Schultheis is an author and journalist who lives in Lawson Hill. He has written books about the wars in Afghanistan (both with the Soviet Union and the U.S.) and the 2003 Iraq War, as well as books about Colorado, the Western United States, and extreme sports such as mountain climbing. …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Historic & Architectural Review Commission - Oct 21 2026 — 2026-10-21
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-21
The October 21 HARC meeting is anchored by the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project — the Town of Telluride's own large-scale development at 860 Black Bear Rd, zoned Accommodations 2. HARC takes up Buildings 1 and 2 as one public hearing item and Buildings 3 and 4 as a second, both continued from August 19. Each application covers new construction outside the Telluride Historic Landmark District exceeding 5,000 square feet of floor area under LUC 7-203.B.2.a.1. Also on the agenda: a payment-in-lieu of parking request for one space at 510 W Columbia Ave/129 N Townsend in the Historic Residential zone, where HARC is asked to support administrative approval. A small-scale new construction application at 785 Primrose Lane on a steep site is also up for review. The 448 Tomboy Road item has been continued to December 16 at the applicant's request, and the 214 S Fir Certificate of Appropriateness Amendment #2 — in the works since at least December 2025 — is being tabled for eight more months.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearings on four buildings in the Town's own large Shandoka redevelopment project.

item.title: [Thu, Oct 22] Water in the West: The Southwest's last, best rivers and how to protect them
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Patagonia Telluride, Telluride Retail Across the Southwest, aridification and challenging politics are impacting our watersheds and threatening our rivers. Join Mike Fiebig, Director of the Southwest River Protection Program at American Rivers, to learn what we can do to protect our local watersheds in the face of a changing climate. Drinks and snacks will be provided! Thanks to our event partners for making this happen: Patagonia Telluride, American Rivers, Dolores River Boating Advocates, and San Juan Citizens Alliance.
